n: After judgment comes joy. The wilderness and dry land will be glad, and the desert will bloom like a flower. Latter-day Saints have seen a fulfillment in the gathering to the western American deserts and in Israel’s restoration.

f.w: the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose

f.g: Probably a crocus or similar desert flower.

n: It will bloom abundantly and sing for joy. The beauty of Lebanon, Carmel, and Sharon — Israel’s greenest places — will be given to it, and people will see the Lord’s glory.
Strengthen weak hands and steady shaky knees. The prophetic message is meant to encourage the discouraged.
Tell the frightened, “Be strong; don’t be afraid! Your God is coming to set things right — He will come and save you.”

f.w: he will come and save you

n: Then the blind will see and the deaf will hear. Jesus pointed to such miracles as evidence of who He was.

f.w: the eyes of the blind shall be opened

n: The lame will leap like deer and the mute will sing for joy, because water will burst out in the wilderness and streams in the desert.

f.w: the lame man leap as an hart
in the wilderness shall waters break out

n: Scorching sand will become a pool and thirsty ground bubbling springs. Where jackals once lived, grass, reeds, and rushes will grow.
A highway will be there, called the Way of Holiness. The unclean will not travel on it, and it will be so clear that even the simple won’t get lost. Latter-day Saints may think of the covenant path.

f.w: though fools, shall not err therein
f.g: Even the simple will not stray.

n: No lion or dangerous beast will be on that road. Only the redeemed will walk there, safe from harm.

The ransomed of the Lord will return to Zion singing, crowned with everlasting joy. Gladness will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee. This verse is repeated in Isaiah 51:11 and echoed in latter-day revelation.

f.w: the ransomed of the LORD shall return
sorrow and sighing shall flee away
